references.text: The Jews discuss and complain about Jesus' claim to be the bread that came down from heaven, just as in verse 41 where they are offended by his words.
A similar reaction occurs where the disciples are offended by Jesus' words, and he asks if they also want to leave, mirroring the offense taken by the Jews in verse 41.
Jesus responds directly to the Jews' offense by pointing out that no one can come to him unless the Father draws them, and that he is the one who has come down from heaven.
Jesus confirms the theme of verse 41 by stating that he has not come to do his own will but the Father's, and that he has come down from heaven.

The precursor to the theme of bread from heaven; the Jews in the wilderness received manna, but in John 6:41 Jesus is the true bread that came down from heaven, which triggers offense among those who do not believe.
